trust_decision.summary: install_packages() must neutralize argument delimiters: every package specifier is allowlisted (extras group restricted to real extra names) and then shell-quoted as one literal token before being spliced into the pip install command string, all inside CodeInterpreter.install_packages.

landing_point.why: The advisory names install_packages(); the validation loop against VALID_PACKAGE_NAME and the unquoted join into the command f-string are the only sink-adjacent lines an engineer would open first.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: CodeInterpreter.execute_command() (src/bedrock_agentcore/tools/code_interpreter_client.py:748-770) and invoke() (:438-466) reach the same executeCommand sink with no neutralization at all, but both are documented raw shell/passthrough APIs, so a solver can reasonably leave them alone as by design and outside the package-installation contract.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate specifiers whose operators are themselves shell metacharacters must keep pip semantics and keep being accepted: pandas>=2.0, numpy<2.0, scipy==1.7.*, pandas[excel]>=1.5. The published fix quotes such tokens (pip install 'pandas>=2.0') rather than rejecting them, so an over-broad fix that bans >, < or extras passes the injection tests but breaks this behaviour; a quoting fix in turn breaks the pre-fix exact-command assertion at tests/bedrock_agentcore/tools/test_code_interpreter_client.py:846 unless it is updated.

O6_input_shapes: bare name, plus names containing dot, underscore and hyphen
wildcard version specifier such as scipy==1.7.*
extras group with one or comma-separated extra names: pandas[security], celery[redis,auth]
extras group followed by a version operator: pandas[excel]>=1.5
extras group content that is not a valid extra name (shell metacharacters, spaces, backticks): now rejected

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an install_packages(..., index_url=None, extra_args=None) variant that appends an index URL or raw flags to the same command string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Private package indexes and pip flags are the most common user request for a sandbox install helper, and a maintainer would naturally extend this existing f-string command rather than start a new path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: uninstall_packages() or run_pip() that reuses the same join of specs and calls execute_command()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already advertises install_packages() as a thin convenience wrapper over executeCommand, so a symmetric uninstall/upgrade helper is the obvious next method and would copy the same join.

O9_family: CWE-88 improper neutralization of argument delimiters in a shell command (OS command argument injection)

O10_build.toolchain: pytest (pyproject testpaths=tests), hatchling build; boto3/botocore/pydantic/starlette/uvicorn at runtime
O10_build.project_tests: tests/bedrock_agentcore/tools/test_code_interpreter_client.py: install_packages tests at 800-915 and TestInstallPackagesAllowlist at 1494-1617 (extras payloads are xfail at the pinned commit); the AWS clients are replaced with MagicMock, so this area runs offline. tests_integ/tools/test_code.py needs a live AgentCore sandbox and is not part of the unit path.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten only the extras group in VALID_PACKAGE_NAME (the payload shape the report shows) and keep the plain join of packages, so a legitimate pandas>=2.0 still reaches the shell as a > redirection and the command-format expectation still fails.
